games.adversary_capabilities: knows sk_cl, ss_cl, ct_cl, pk_cl, label; PQ shared secret truncated to n bits
games.oracle_access: 64 combiner evaluations per trial (distinct guesses of the n-bit secret)
games.winning_condition: b' == b for K_b (b=0: combine(...), b=1: uniform)
games.expected_win_bound: IND wins <= 1/2 + Q/2^(n+1); real-world hit rate = Q/2^n (measured, slope vs n fitted)
games.mechanism: combine(): the unknown n-bit ss_pq enters the hash; without it K is a fresh RO output
games.assumption_invoked: H (SHA3-256 in combine()) modelled as a random oracle / PRF (GHP18 Thm 3.1; X-Wing 2024); independence of the two KEM components (keys, randomness, implementation)

games.adversary_capabilities: knows sk_pq, ss_pq, ct_cl, pk_cl, label; classical shared secret truncated to n bits
games.expected_win_bound: as S6-A with the roles swapped
games.mechanism: combine() is symmetric in which component survives
games.assumption_invoked: H (SHA3-256 in combine()) modelled as a random oracle / PRF (GHP18 Thm 3.1; X-Wing 2024); independence of the two KEM components (keys, randomness, implementation)

games.game_name: NEGATIVE: correlated randomness across the two components
games.adversary_capabilities: public data only (pk_cl, ct_cl); knows both components share one n_seed-bit seed
games.oracle_access: offline: 2^n_seed table seed -> ct_cl; online: one lookup + 4 hashes per trial
games.expected_win_bound: combiner theorem gives Q/2^256 = 2^(n_seed-256) ONLY IF components are independent; hypothesis violated -> no bound applies; measured 1.0
games.mechanism: none: the combiner cannot manufacture independence; fix is at the RNG/implementation layer
games.assumption_invoked: independence of the two KEM components (keys, randomness, implementation) -- shown NECESSARY, not just sufficient

games.adversary_capabilities: MITM edits the ClientHello group list in transit; may guess a t-bit Finished tag; quantum variant: breaks X25519 online and learns ss_cl
games.winning_condition: client completes with a group weaker than its best offer
games.expected_win_bound: bound transcript: 2^-t per Finished guess (t=256 -> 0); unbound: 1 (downgrade succeeds); bound + quantum X25519 break: 1 unless client refuses Cat 0 (policy, not binding)
games.mechanism: key schedule hashes the exact ClientHello bytes as sent; Finished = HMAC(K, transcript hash)
games.assumption_invoked: HMAC-SHA3 is a PRF; the negotiated key is unknown to the adversary

games.adversary_capabilities: chooses typecode, root record, signature and version; own key sets under n=24, n=16, toy n=1
games.oracle_access: verifier as a black box; unlimited keygen
games.winning_condition: verifier installs a root record not signed under the pinned parameter set, or an older one
games.expected_win_bound: strict: 2^-256 per keygen (Grover 2^128 x 2^18 gates); lax prefix: 2^-(8n) per keygen -> n=24: 2^114 gates, n=16: 2^82 gates (both below QPT-128); toy n=1: 2^-8 measured
games.mechanism: pinned typecode checked before parsing; full-length root compare; monotonic root version
games.assumption_invoked: ROM immutability (verifier code and pinned typecode/root/counter cannot be changed); second-preimage resistance of the n=32 hash

games.game_name: algorithm agility ledger + QPT-128 gate margins
games.adversary_capabilities: reference attacks of the v1.43 ledger; Grover with 2^18 gates per hash query
games.expected_win_bound: every target Cat 5; no deployed entry passes; margins n=128: -46, n=192: -14, n=256: +18 bits
games.mechanism: per-layer migration ledger; ROM layer chosen Cat 5 at manufacture because it cannot rotate
games.assumption_invoked: v1.43 gate accounting (2^18 gates/query); category reference attack costs

SLH-DSA-256s-MTL (n=32) ladder, canonical-order shards of 2^12, NSEC + multiproof

same_game_tls_session: union bound over 2 sub-events of goal 'break TLS session'
independent_layers: refused: bounds span 2 attacker goals ['forge DNSSEC answer', 'forge firmware root']; a union bound is only defined for sub-events of one game
composition.rule:
Union bound over per-layer advantage bounds (log2 values), returned ONLY when
    every bound belongs to the same attacker goal inside one security game.

    Why the refusal: Pr[A or B] <= Pr[A] + Pr[B] is a statement about two events in
    ONE probability space -- one experiment, one adversary, one winning condition.
    'Break this TLS session' = (break the KEM) or (forge the authentication) is such
    a pair: same session, same adversary, so their bounds add.  A DNSSEC forger and
    a firmware forger are different experiments with different adversaries and
    different winning conditions; the sum of their bounds is not the probability of
    any event and answers no question (it is neither the system's failure
    probability nor a per-layer margin).  Independent layers are reported side by
    side -- the weakest link is the max -- and never added.
    Returns (log2_bound, reason) or (None, reason).

untestable_assumptions.assumption: random-oracle / PRF modelling of the combiner hash (SHA3-256 in combine())
untestable_assumptions.why_untestable: the reduction treats H as a random oracle; no experiment on outputs can separate "SHA3 is a PRF" from "SHA3 is a random oracle" -- the games measure scaling under the model, not the model

untestable_assumptions.assumption: independence of the two KEM components (key material, randomness, implementation)
untestable_assumptions.why_untestable: S6-C shows the bound collapses when violated, but whether a deployment shares a DRBG, entropy pool or code path is a property of the implementation, not of the algorithm

untestable_assumptions.assumption: ROM immutability: verifier code, pinned typecode, root and version counter cannot be altered
untestable_assumptions.why_untestable: a mask-ROM / OTP property of the silicon; software can only assume the verifier runs as written

untestable_assumptions.assumption: ToyKEM stands in for ML-KEM-1024 / X25519; IND-CCA of ML-KEM (Module-LWE) and the v1.43 category gate costs
untestable_assumptions.why_untestable: lattice hardness and the reference attack costs are inputs from the QPT-128 ledger, not re-derived
